paper_title: Measuring Layer-wise Intrinsic Dimensionality of FFNs in LLMs via PCA

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Modern large language models (LLMs) keep the feed-forward network (FFN) intermediate width identical across every layer, a convention inherited from the original Transformer. Yet mechanistic work suggests layers at different depths do qualitatively different work, raising a natural question: are their capacity demands also non-uniform, and if so, can a fixed parameter budget be allocated more wisely than uniformly? To probe this, we apply principal component analysis (PCA) to the input of each FFN down-projection and measure, for every layer, its intrinsic dimensionality as the smallest number of principal components needed to reconstruct the activation up to a fixed cosine similarity. Scanning 58 open-weight LLMs spanning 14 families and 70M to 72B parameters, we find a recurring middle-heavy profile in which middle layers carry higher intrinsic dimensionality than edge layers; the profile is robust to the calibration corpus, even across English and Chinese, and is largely preserved through post-training fine-tuning. As a direct test that this signal is structurally meaningful, we use it to guide width pruning in a knowledge-distilled student under a matched parameter budget: the PCA-guided allocation outperforms the uniform-width convention by +2.3 points on Qwen3-8B and +2.5 on Qwen2.5-3B, while lower-dispersion teachers show smaller gaps (+0.9 on Gemma-3-4B, +0.5 on LLaMA-3-8B), and a budget-matched inverted control does worst on all four teachers. Across these four teachers, the size of the gap tracks how unevenly the teacher's intrinsic dimensionality is distributed across layers (a single-number summary we call $σ_{99}$), and the advantage persists through downstream supervised fine-tuning. Code is available at https://github.com/naver-ai/lidf.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: Every mainstream LLM [Touvron et al., 2023, Yang et al., 2024a, Jiang et al., 2023] applies the same FFN intermediate dimension to every transformer block, convention inherited from the original Transformer [Vaswani et al., 2017]. This uniformity is computationally convenient but embeds strong implicit assumption: that every layer performs representational work of the same complexity. growing body of mechanistic work [Geva et al., 2021, Meng et al., 2022, Dai et al., 2022, Geva et al., 2022] suggests this assumption does not hold: layers at different depths process qualitatively different information. Yet whether the per-layer capacity demand is also non-uniform, and whether deviating from uniform width yields measurable benefits, has not been directly characterized at scale. We explore this gap by introducing simple, data-agnostic measurement protocol for layer-wise intrinsic dimensionality and by validating its predictions in controlled width-pruning experiment. Specifically, we hook the input to each FFNs down-projection, the last intermediate activation of the layer in both gated (SwiGLU) [Shazeer, 2020] and non-gated (Gaussian Error Linear Unit, GELU) [Hendrycks and Gimpel, 2016] FFNs. We apply PCA [Jolliffe, 2002] to it and define dθ as the smallest rank at which the cosine similarity between the activation and its top-d PCA reconstruction 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026). reaches threshold θ. The result is per-layer integer, comparable across layers and architectures, that requires only single forward pass on small unlabeled corpus. Three observations emerge from 58-model scan covering 14 families at 70M72B parameters: (i) the per-layer dθ profile is recurringly middle-heavy: most models exhibit higher dθ at intermediate depth and lower dθ at the edges; (ii) the profile is largely robust to the calibration corpus, including across English and Chinese inputs (per-layer Pearson 0.94 on Qwen3-8B [Yang et al., 2025]); (iii) the layer-wise dispersion σ99 := stdl(dθ,l/Dl) at the default threshold θ = 0.99, single-number summary of how unevenly intrinsic dimensionality is distributed across layers, is model-internal property that is approximately preserved through post-training such as supervised fine-tuning (SFT). As functional test of the measurement, we use dθ directly as width-allocation rule for student trained by knowledge distillation (KD) [Hinton et al., 2015]. Three students with budget-matched FFN allocationsPCA-guided (each layers width set to dθ,l), UNIFORM (flat width, current convention), and INVERTED (point-wise mirror around uniform, an adversarial control)are distilled from the same teacher with identical optimizer, data, and learning-rate schedule. On the two high-σ99 teachers (Qwen2.5-3B [Qwen Team, 2024] and Qwen3-8B), PCA outperforms UNIFORM by +2.3 to +2.5 percentage points (pp) and INVERTED by +4.6 to +5.5 pp on five-task average; on the lower-σ99 Gemma-3-4B [Gemma Team, 2025] and LLaMA-3-8B [Grattafiori et al., 2024] the gaps against UNIFORM are smaller (+0.5 to +0.9 pp). The advantage tracks layer-wise dispersion (σ99) across the four teachers and is negligible at 1.5B and below; downstream SFT round preserves the ordering, with PCA UNIFORM at +11.0 pp on ARC-Challenge (ARC-C) [Clark et al., 2018], +4.9 pp on MMLU [Hendrycks et al., 2021], and +3.0 pp on GSM8K [Cobbe et al., 2021]. Contributions. 1. Measurement protocol. We define layer-wise intrinsic dimensionality dθ for FFN downprojection input activations via PCA combined with cosine-similarity threshold (2). The protocol is data-agnostic and label-free. 2. Empirical characterization across 58 LLMs. We document recurring middle-heavy profile, calibration-data robustness (Pearson 0.94 across all pairs of 5 English corpora and Chinese SkyPile [Wei et al., 2023]), pretraining-trajectory growth phase in 20 of 21 trajectories across six families, and post-training stability of the layer-wise dispersion (3). 3. Functional validation: controlled KD. PCA-guided width allocation outperforms budgetmatched uniform allocation on four teachers at moderate-to-large scale; the inverted control falls below the uniform allocation; the advantage persists through SFT (4).

sections.title: 3 What dθ Measures: Empirical Characterization
sections.content: We scanned 58 LLMs spanning 14 families and 70M72B parameters with the protocol of 2. Four findings emerge. 3.1 The profile is robust to calibration data, language, and measurement site We test whether dθ depends on the choice of calibration corpus along two axes: distributional variation within single language, and variation across languages. On Qwen3-8B, we measure dθ using six 100K-token corpora: five English (SlimPajama, MMLU, ARC-C, HellaSwag [Zellers et al., 2019], WikiText [Merity et al., 2017]) and one Chinese (SkyPile [Wei et al., 2023]). Across the five English corpora, all pairwise per-layer Pearson correlations lie in [0.953, 0.990] (mean 0.975), indicating that dθ is largely insensitive to the textual domain of the calibration data. stronger test is cross-language: per-layer correlations between Chinese SkyPile and each English corpus lie in [0.941, 0.993] (mean 0.973), comparable to the all-English pairwise correlations. The lowest pairwise correlation across all 15 pairs is 0.941 (Chinese SkyPile vs. HellaSwag), reflecting the outlier commonsense distribution of HellaSwag rather than the language gap. sections.title: 4 Validation: Controlled Width Pruning under KD
sections.content: We treat the 3-way KD experiment as validation of the measurement protocol. The primary prediction is that PCA, with per-layer widths set to d0.99, outperforms budget-matched flat allocation UNIFORM; an ablation at the tighter θ = 0.97 budget is reported in Appendix A. We additionally include an inverted allocation INVERTED (the per-layer mirror of PCA around uniform) as falsifiability check: finding of INVERTED UNIFORM would be consistent with the weaker hypothesis that any non-uniform allocation helps, while the observed INVERTED < UNIFORM on all four teachers identifies the shape of the allocation, not its non-uniformity, as the relevant signal. 4.1 Setup Models. We use four pretrained-only (base) teachers at moderate-to-large scale: Qwen2.5-3B, Qwen3-8B, Gemma-3-4B, and LLaMA-3-8B. For each teacher we distill three students under the same KD recipe. Allocations. Let be the number of transformer layers and Dl the teachers FFN intermediate width at layer l. For each teacher, we fix the students total FFN parameter budget to the sum of the teachers measured per-layer dθ values: = (cid:80) dθ,l at θ = 0.99. The budget is therefore not tuning hyperparameter but direct consequence of the threshold choice. Within budget we construct three layer-width vectors: PCA: wl = dθ,l at θ = 0.99, rounded to multiples of 128. UNIFORM: wl B/L. INVERTED: wl = 2 unil pcal (the per-layer mirror of PCA around UNIFORM), clipped to [128, Dl] and rescaled to B. All three allocations match up to rounding, and any residual (at most +1.3%, for UNIFORM or INVERTED) favors the baseline; Figure 4 visualizes the per-layer width vectors for each teacher. Initialization, distillation, and evaluation. We initialize each student via Minitron-style importance pruning [Muralidharan et al., 2024], scoring per-neuron importance by absolute activation magnitude over 128 SlimPajama calibration sequences of length 2,048, and retaining within each layer the top-scoring neurons up to that layers allocated width. [2025b] (α = 8), redundancy signal based on the cosine similarity between each layers input and output. PCA-EV is comparable to PCA on Qwen2.5-3B but falls below it on Gemma-3-4B, and SLIMLLM trails PCA on both teachers, most on MMLU. The cosine readout keeps width on such layers and appears more robust across the two teachers. The rules above all read profile from the model being pruned; further question is whether any sufficiently middle-heavy profile would do. sections.title: 5 Discussion and Limitations
sections.content: What drives the family-level σ99 signatures? σ99 shows substantial association with model family and spans more than 2 across families (Figure 2: 0.180.21 for Qwen2.5 3B32B and Qwen3 8B32B vs. LLaMA 0.080.11). Identifying the responsible recipe ingredient would require iso-architecture iso-data ablations that public checkpoints cannot provide, and the same limitation restricts the σ99-vs-gap pattern to the four teachers tested (σ99 [0.105, 0.192]); iso-family iso-scale variants across wider σ99 range would help disentangle recipe from σ99. Limitations. Two limitations concern scale and deployment. Our runs cover 1.574.2B training tokens; whether the advantage persists at Minitron-scale budgets (70100B) is untested. nonuniform student also carries serving cost: in our vLLM [Kwon et al., 2023] integration the trained PCA student is 5.3% slower than UNIFORM at 0.4% parameter difference (Appendix F). 9 Toward dθ-guided width re-allocation beyond KD. Two natural extensions are re-shaping the same pretrained model under preserved budget with continued pretraining, and selective capacity augmentation at high-dθ layers of an already-trained model, motivated by the observation that σ99 changes little after pretraining (3.4). Whether the advantage persists under either scheme is the top future ablation. layer-output perturbation or pruning-sensitivity study would further test whether high-dθ layers are also more capacity-sensitive.

sections.title: 6 Related Work
sections.content: Functional heterogeneity of FFN layers. FFN layers act as key-value memories [Geva et al., 2021] whose updates promote vocabulary concepts [Geva et al., 2022]; causal tracing localizes factual associations to middle multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) [Meng et al., 2022], and Dai et al. [2022] identify knowledge neurons in BERT [Devlin et al., 2019]. These studies suggest that FFN layers at different depths perform qualitatively different functions; our dθ provides complementary, quantitative signal of how many activation directions each layer uses. Width-aware compression and pruning. WANDA [Sun et al., 2024] and SparseGPT [Frantar and Alistarh, 2023] induce unstructured sparsity, and LLM-Pruner [Ma et al., 2023], Sheared LLaMA [Xia et al., 2024], ShortGPT [Men et al., 2025], SliceGPT [Ashkboos et al., 2024] and Olica [He and Lin, 2025] remove neuron groups, heads, layers or dimensions; none of them allocates per-layer FFN width from measured intrinsic-dimensionality profile under fixed budget. SlimLLM [Guo et al., 2025b] does allocate per-layer ratio, and we compare against its rule in 4.3. W-PCA [Wang, 2025] counts PCA components of FFN states in untrained BERT-scale networks as zero-shot neural architecture search (NAS) proxy; we measure trained LLMs and use the profile directly as the allocation. Minitron [Muralidharan et al., 2024] couples width pruning with distillation under uniform ratio; we adopt its recipe and replace the uniform allocation with dθ. Closest in motivation, Ikeda et al. [2025] report binary middle-heavy FFN allocation trained from scratch on single architecture family at 285M1.2B parameters; we differ in (i) producing non-binary dθ per layer and (ii) validating with controlled KD experiment that isolates width allocation from training procedure. Effective rank and intrinsic dimensionality. Effective rank [Roy and Vetterli, 2007] and nonlinear intrinsic-dimension estimators [Ansuini et al., 2019] characterize layer representations; Aghajanyan et al. [2021] instead use parameter-space intrinsic dimension to explain fine-tuning. Ansuini et al. [2019] report hunchback profile in convolutional neural networks (CNNs), in which intrinsic dimensionality first increases and then progressively decreases toward the output, and note that linear estimates such as PCA do not recover it; our PCA-based measure recovers an analogous middle-heavy profile in LLM FFNs. Shenk et al. [2019] and Richter et al. [2021] define layer saturation as the share of dimensions needed to reach fixed cumulative explained variance and use it to diagnose overprovisioned layers during training. Our dθ is in this family but specialized to FFN down-projection input activations, and uses cosine-similarity threshold rather than explained variance, motivated by the direction-additive way in which FFN outputs enter the residual stream; it separates from saturation on layers dominated by single direction, where the cosine readout retains substantially more width (4.3, Appendix E).

sections.title: 7 Conclusion
sections.content: We define dθ via cosine-thresholded PCA on the FFN down-projection input and document recurring middle-heavy, calibration-robust, post-training-stable profile across 58 LLMs spanning 14 families from 70M to 72B parameters. The single-number dispersion σ99 derived from the profile is modelinternal property that survives the shift from English to Chinese calibration and changes little across post-training fine-tuning. We validate the signal in 3-way KD experiment in which budget-matched PCA-guided allocation beats UNIFORM on four teachers and budget-matched INVERTED control does worst, with the magnitude of the advantage tracking σ99 across teachers and persisting through downstream supervised fine-tuning.
